decisions.name: Theorem 7.1.6 Brownian paths are not Lipschitz
decisions.reason: Sharp failure at exponent one half is a later path-properties topic; this pair establishes existence and positive Holder regularity only.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Durrett Theorem 7.1.6, printed pp.358–359, proves pointwise failure of Lipschitz continuity and hence nowhere differentiability; its complete probability estimate was read. The recorded reason instead calls it sharp failure at exponent one half, which is a different claim. PT-18 and the current page retain positive Holder regularity below one half, scaling, inversion, and Wiener measure. Owner must reconcile the inaccurate reason and decide whether this construction-adjacent negative result remains excluded; no endpoint theorem was silently substituted or added.

decisions.name: Theorem 5.2.7 reflection principle for random walks
decisions.reason: This discrete random-walk reflection result belongs with later hitting-time computations, not the assigned kernel and construction interface.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Durrett Theorem 5.2.7 is a reflection inequality for sums of iid symmetric increments, presented after the strong Markov theorem. The current kernel page retains thm-discrete-strong-markov-property and the post-hitting restart corollary, but its general measurable-state construction/martingale interface does not assert that symmetric random-walk inequality. This downstream distributional computation can remain excluded from the selected pair.

decisions.name: Theorem 5.2.6 iterated return-time decomposition
decisions.reason: This result starts the later recurrence and return-time theory explicitly excluded from the assigned general-kernel construction page.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 lead: Read Durrett Theorem 5.2.6 and its complete induction, printed p.278: the kth return probability equals the initial hitting probability times the (k-1)st power of the return probability. It consumes strong Markov and begins recurrence analysis. Current thm-discrete-strong-markov-property remains present, while the selected kernel pair does not claim recurrence classification. Exclusion stands.
